record.title: Lei and Ren detail a Navier–Stokes blowup profile construction with admissible stress and flat remainder
record.summary: Zhen Lei and Xiao Ren present a detailed construction of smooth axisymmetric self-similar profiles related to OpenAI's proposed forced Navier–Stokes blowup proof. In the arXiv record, v1 was submitted on 28 September and v2 revised on 29 September; the authors describe the work as expository and say it will not be submitted to a journal. They report matching five profile moments, constructing an admissible stress and obtaining a remainder that vanishes to infinite order on fixed similarity sectors. The paper is Part I: it identifies cancellation of the remaining residual by oscillatory pulses as a companion Part II step. It therefore supplies a bounded profile-construction result and an inspectable stage of the argument, not a completed finite-time blowup theorem or resolution of the Clay problem.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Lei and Ren submitted Part I of a paper describing a self-similar profile construction for forced Navier–Stokes on 28 September 2026; arXiv records a v2 revision dated 29 September 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report smooth axisymmetric profiles whose associated stress and radial shear satisfy an admissible cone condition, with a residual consisting of a stress-divergence term and a remainder flat to infinite order on fixed similarity sectors.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors identify cancellation of the residual by oscillatory pulses as the work of a companion Part II; Part I does not itself establish a complete finite-time blowup theorem or resolve the Clay problem.

evidence_gaps.description: The oscillatory-pulse residual-correction companion paper named in Part I was not found in the exact-title arXiv search; its status outside arXiv is unknown.
No independent specialist audit of the Part I profile construction or its admissible-cone and flat-remainder estimates was established.

Part I states simultaneous compatibility requirements and the candidate's prior review notes that their joint satisfiability is not guaranteed by choosing a single parameter large; this load-bearing condition has not been independently checked here.
The relation between the external exposition and the full OpenAI manuscript has not been independently checked line by line; the authors describe Part I as a readable version of one component.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported admissible-stress profile construction and compatibility conditions are correct, they provide a material and inspectable component of a proposed finite-time singularity construction for forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes. Its consequence is notable for specialist proof review, while Part I leaves residual cancellation to a companion step and does not establish the full theorem.
limitations: Part I constructs profiles and controls a residual; its abstract explicitly assigns cancellation by oscillatory pulses to a companion Part II.
The exact-title arXiv search did not find the named Part II, but author or institutional repositories outside arXiv were not exhaustively searched.
No independent specialist review or formal verification of the Part I construction was established in this activation.
The paper states simultaneous compatibility requirements; whether the full set of load-bearing conditions is satisfiable requires specialist audit.
The authors frame the work as a readable account of a profile-construction portion of OpenAI's manuscript; it is not independent confirmation of the complete theorem.
The current arXiv record labels the paper expository and says it will not be submitted to a journal; this does not itself settle the mathematical correctness of its construction.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report a smooth profile field with admissible stress, five matched moments and a residual remainder flat to infinite order on fixed similarity sectors.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not applicable to the mathematical claim; no compute-cost result is claimed.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public Part I preprint and its stated construction are accessible; the mathematical validity of all lemmas and compatibility conditions was not independently verified in this review.
technical.implementation_status: Public preprint; an exact-title arXiv search found Part I and its statement that residual cancellation is assigned to a companion Part II. This does not rule out publication elsewhere.
technical.mechanism: Constructs smooth axisymmetric self-similar profiles by matching five moments across core, transition and exterior regions, then adds lower-order corrections; the residual is expressed as a divergence-form stress plus a flat remainder.
technical.regime: Forced incompressible three-dimensional Navier–Stokes in an axisymmetric self-similar blowup construction; Part I addresses profile construction, not cancellation of the final residual into an exact solution.
technical.reproducibility: No independent line-by-line proof review or machine formalization was established in this activation. The joint compatibility premise and complete Part II correction remain key review targets.
technical.strongest_baseline: This is a proof-construction paper rather than a benchmark comparison. Its stated target is the profile-construction component of OpenAI's proposed proof; an independent specialist audit is not established here.

brief.title: Lei and Ren detail a Navier–Stokes blowup profile construction with admissible stress and flat remainder
brief.why_it_matters: A detailed external construction of a technically central profile component makes a highly consequential proposed proof more inspectable and identifies which remaining step carries the theorem-level burden. If its construction and compatibility conditions withstand specialist review, it could aid evaluation of the broader Navier–Stokes claim. The article itself says a companion residual-correction step is still required, so it cannot be treated as a proof of the Millennium problem.
